stem: Eight people P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W sit in one row in seats numbered 1 (leftmost) to 8 (rightmost), all facing forward. R is third to the left of V. P sits at one of the two ends. Exactly one person sits between P and R. S sits immediately to the right of V. Q sits somewhere to the right of S. T is not adjacent to R. U does not sit at either end. W sits immediately to the right of P. Who sits in seat 5?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Chaining V=R+3, |P-R|=2, P at an end forces P=1, R=3, V=6, S=7. W=P+1=2, leaving U and T for seats 4 and 5; T cannot be adjacent to R (seat 3), so U=4 and T=5. Q=8 is right of S. The whole row P,W,R,U,T,V,S,Q is the unique fit, with T in seat 5.
U sits in seat 4, not 5. Putting U in seat 5 drops the clue that T may not be adjacent to R; honouring it pushes U left of T.
Reading 'third to the left' as third to the right mirrors the frame and slides W rightward into seat 5; W actually sits in seat 2 next to P.
Anchoring the R-V block at the right end instead of using P at the left makes S land left of centre, dropping Q into seat 5; in the valid row Q is forced to seat 8.

explanation: Number seats 1 to 8. 'R third to the left of V' means seat(V) = seat(R) + 3. 'P at an end' with 'exactly one person between P and R' means |seat(P) - seat(R)| = 2. P=8 would need R=6, then V=9 which does not exist, so P=1 and R=3, giving V=6. 'S immediately right of V' puts S in seat 7. 'W immediately right of P' puts W in seat 2. Remaining seats 4 and 5 take U and T: T cannot be adjacent to R (seat 3), so T avoids seat 4, giving T=5 and U=4. Q is the last person, seat 8, which is right of S as required, and U is interior. The unique arrangement is P, W, R, U, T, V, S, Q, so seat 5 is T.

explanation_sections.punchline: The fixed gap seat(V)=seat(R)+3 plus 'P at an end, one between P and R' pins P=1, R=3, V=6 immediately; then 'T not adjacent to R' decides seats 4 and 5, giving T in seat 5.
explanation_sections.approach: Archetype move: turn every relative clue into an arithmetic seat equation (V=R+3, |P-R|=2, S=V+1, W=P+1), solve the equations to lock the skeleton, then let the lone soft clue (T not next to R) break the final tie between the two open seats.
explanation_sections.lesson: In fixed-gap row puzzles, anchor first on the pair with the largest forced gap and on the end-seat clue; together they usually fix three or four seats before any negative clue is touched.
explanation_sections.timing: 150-170 seconds. Fastest elimination: option Q dies at once because Q must sit to the right of S, and S is already deep on the right, so Q cannot occupy seat 5.
